title: Multivariate Calculus: Visual Guide
outline: 1. Slice To Slope | the familiar one-variable tangent line reappearing on a surface: freeze y (or x) and f(x,y) = x^3 y^2 becomes an ordinary curve whose slope is the partial derivative, checked live against the h = 0.001 limit and used to build the tangent plane | a partial derivative is no new machinery - it is the ordinary derivative of the curve you get by holding the other input still, and two such tangent lines fix a unique tangent plane

2. Partials To Gradient | a contour map with the two partial derivatives shown as signed bars and stacked into the gradient arrow at a draggable point, for x^3 y^2, a bowl and a saddle, with the level-curve direction drawn perpendicular to it | the gradient is a VECTOR of first partials that points along steepest ascent with length equal to the climb rate, so -grad f is steepest descent and perpendicular to it means no change, not descent

3. Unit Vector Rule | grad f . u-hat computed live on the unit circle while you stretch the direction vector, showing the correct directional derivative beside the un-normalised dot product and the divide-by-|grad f| variant | a direction is a heading, not a distance: normalise u before the dot product, and read every which-way question off D = |grad f| cos(phi), bounded by plus and minus |grad f| and zero at right angles

4. Cooling Fastest | a room with two heaters where you choose a heading and a step length, ranking your cooling rate against the best possible -|grad T| and comparing the tangent plane's predicted temperature change with the room's actual one | moving opposite the gradient gives the largest decrease PER UNIT OF DISTANCE, and only for a small step - shrink the step and prediction meets reality, enlarge it and the linear guess falls apart

5. Hessian Decides | the Hessian of f = a x^2 + b y^2 + c x y with its curvature curve u^T H u swept over every direction, its two extremes marked as the eigenvalues, and the verdict switching between minimum, maximum, saddle and inconclusive | the eigenvalues are the best and worst curvature available, so all positive means positive definite, concave up and a local minimum - the multivariable form of the f'' > 0 test, with a nonzero mixed partial being perfectly normal
